title: Ninety Days from Empty
subtitle: In 1997 Apple was losing a lot of money and making too many products. Then its old boss came back with a very short list.

vocab.def: A thing that a company makes and sells.
vocab.ex: Apple made dozens of different products.

vocab.def: A person or company that wants to win against you.
To put money into something because you hope to get more back later.
vocab.ex: Microsoft invested 150 million dollars in Apple.

vocab.def: To make something smaller or stop part of it.
vocab.ex: Jobs cut most of the products.

vocab.def: The money a company keeps when it earns more than it spends.
vocab.ex: In 1998 Apple made a profit again.

vocab.def: When a company spends more money than it earns. The opposite of a profit.
vocab.ex: The loss in 1997 was about one billion dollars.

vocab.def: To give all your attention to one thing. Focus is also the noun.
vocab.ex: Apple decided to focus on just four computers.

vocab.def: To come back or go back to a place.
vocab.ex: Steve Jobs returned to Apple in 1997.

vocab.def: How something looks and how it is made.
vocab.ex: People loved the colourful design of the iMac.

vocab.def: Doing very well; getting the result you wanted.
vocab.ex: The iPhone was one of the most successful products ever.

items: Barcelona's biggest ___ in football is Real Madrid.
My uncle wants to ___ his savings in a small restaurant.
Good news! The café made a ___ this year — it earned more than it spent.
She left the company in 2010, but she ___ in 2015 as the new boss.
Please turn off the music. I need to ___ on this exam.

vocab_discuss: Which company makes your phone? Why did you choose it?
Do you buy things because of their design, or only because they work well?
Have you ever had too many choices in a shop? What did you do?

story.heading: Part 1 — Too many products
paras: Steve Jobs started Apple with a friend in 1976.
But in 1985, after a big fight with the board, Jobs left his own company.
In the 1990s, Apple had big problems. Most people bought computers with Microsoft Windows, not Apple computers.
Apple tried to answer by making more and more products. There were many computers with confusing numbers, and also printers, cameras and a small handheld computer.
Customers did not understand the difference between all the computers. Shop workers did not understand either.
Apple's software was also old. It tried to make new software, but the project failed.
In late 1996 Apple bought NeXT, Jobs's new company, for about 400 million dollars. The deal gave Apple new software. And it brought Jobs back.
In 1997 Apple had a loss of about one billion dollars. Jobs later said the company was about ninety days from running out of money.
tf: In the 1990s, Apple made only a few simple products.
Apple bought NeXT because it needed new software.
discuss: Why is it a problem when a company makes too many products?
Apple bought a company and got its old boss back. Is it a good idea to bring back an old leader? Why?

story.heading: Part 2 — Help from a rival, and four boxes
paras: In August 1997, Jobs spoke at a big Apple event. He had surprising news.
Microsoft, Apple's biggest rival, was going to invest 150 million dollars in Apple. It also promised to make its Office software for Apple computers for five years.
When Bill Gates, Microsoft's boss, appeared on the big screen, some people in the audience booed.
But the news was important. It told customers that Apple was not going to die.
Then Jobs cut most of the products. He drew a simple picture with four boxes.
One computer for home and one for professionals. One desktop and one laptop for each. That was all.
In 1998 Apple showed the iMac. It was a colourful computer that was easy to connect to the internet.
People loved the design. It sold very well, and in 1998 Apple made a profit again.
tf: Microsoft gave money to Apple in 1997.
Everybody in the audience was happy to see Bill Gates.
After the cuts, Apple planned to make four main types of computer.
discuss: Would you accept help from your biggest rival? What are the dangers?
Jobs made the plan very simple: four boxes. Why is a simple plan powerful?

story.heading: Part 3 — From four boxes to everything
paras: After the iMac, Apple made the iPod in 2001, the iPhone in 2007 and the iPad in 2010.
Steve Jobs died in 2011. Tim Cook became the new boss.
Since then, Apple has become one of the most valuable companies in the world. It has been worth more than three trillion dollars.
Many people tell this story with one simple lesson: focus. Do a few things very well.
But the story is not so simple. Microsoft's help was very important. And Jobs was the founder, so people accepted big cuts from him.
Today Apple has many products again: phones, computers, watches, headphones, and a lot of services like music, TV and payments.
In 2024 Apple reportedly stopped a secret car project after about ten years.
So here is the question. Can a very big company still focus? Or was focus only the answer for a company in trouble?
tf: Tim Cook became Apple's boss after Steve Jobs died.
Today Apple makes only four products.
The story says Microsoft's help was not important at all.
discuss: Is Apple a focused company today? Why or why not?
Apple stopped its car project after about ten years. Was that a failure or a good decision?
Tell the story again in six sentences. Use: left · lost · came back · cut · has become · has made.

grammar.name: present perfect or past simple
grammar.heading: Present perfect or past simple? — Apple lost or Apple has become
explain: This story has two times: the finished past (1985, 1997, 2011) and a time that continues until now.
Past simple — finished time, often with a date: I moved to this city in 2019.
Present perfect (have / has + past participle) — from the past until now, or life experience with no date: I have lived here since 2019. · Have you ever been to Japan?
Signal words: yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago → past simple. since, for, ever, never, yet, already → often present perfect.
Careful: never use the present perfect with a finished time. I saw him yesterday. (NOT I have seen him yesterday)

practice.heading: Complete the sentences
practice.intro: Put the verb in brackets into the past simple or the present perfect.
items: Apple ___ about one billion dollars in 1997. (lose)
Apple ___ many different products since the first iPhone. (make)
Steve Jobs ___ back to Apple in 1997. (come)
I ___ an Apple watch. I don't really want one. (never / use)
My brother ___ his phone for five years, and it still works. (have)

fix.heading: Find the mistake
items: I have bought my laptop last year.
She works at this company since 2020.
How long do you know your best friend?
We have watched a great film yesterday.
answers: I bought my laptop last year. (finished time = past simple)
Steve Jobs died in 2011. (a date = past simple)
She has worked at this company since 2020. (since = present perfect)
How long have you known your best friend? (until now = present perfect)
We watched a great film yesterday. (yesterday = past simple)

speak.label: 1 · Tell the story
paras: Tell me the story of Apple in 1997 in your own words. Six or seven sentences is enough.

speak.label: 2 · Your life until now
paras: Tell me three things you did in the past, with a date.
Then tell me three things you have done in your life, with no date. Use ever or never once.

speak.label: 3 · Too many things
paras: Think of something in your life with too many choices: a menu, your wardrobe, your phone apps, your work.
What would you cut first?

speak.label: 4 · A product you love
paras: Tell me about a product you have used for a long time.
When did you buy it? Why do you still use it?

final: Is it better to do a few things very well, or many things quite well? Why?
Should a company ever accept money from its biggest rival? When?
If you were Apple's boss today, what would you stop making? Why?
